surfBiteReport: The most recent available reports are from roughly 10–21 days ago, so treat this as a general current-season picture rather than a real-time snapshot. Water temperature at the surf zone is running 85°F. Pompano has been the headline surf species across the entire stretch from 30A through Panama City Beach, with multiple reports of solid catches in July — scouting for clean, sargassum-free water is the key, as June grass and sargassum have periodically fouled the surf zone and shut the bite down when thick. Redfish have also shown up nearshore in the surf and close to passes, with schools reported feeding aggressively on falling tides around the full moon period. Spanish mackerel have been active as well, hitting lures with virtually every cast during some recent sessions. Sand fleas, peeled shrimp, and FishBites in ghost shrimp or chartreuse scents have been the go-to surf baits for pompano and whiting; jack crevalle schools are also cruising the beach and can provide unexpected drag-ripping action.
